messages:
olivia: Heads-up — planning a blue->green traffic shift for router-prod in eu-west at 11:30 UTC. Target is 50% for 10m, then 100% if healthy.

sam: noted. what's the pin/version for the green?

olivia: green is running v2.4.1 (model pin: inference-qa-2026-04). No schema changes.

mike: can we do region-by-region or global? I'd prefer region-by-region to reduce blast.

olivia: region-by-region. eu-west first, then us-west, then us-east. We'll use floating-route shifts — 25% steps -> 50% probe -> 100%.

nisha: checklist: warm caches, priming requests, backend pools scaled x1.5, canary logs forwarded to sled. Also set circuit-breaker thresholds to 2xx-only pass for 5m.

ben: add rollback criteria: error rate > 1.5% sustained for 3m OR p95 latency > 300ms over baseline +50ms. If triggered, immediate drain and shift back to blue.

olivia: agreed. also watch auth failures and redis 5xx. If any auth spike, we do manual rollback.

deploy-bot: deploy started by @olivia — route shift job id=shft-2060012345. Step 1: prepare green pools.

deploy-bot: green pool scale ok. priming requests sent (100). KV cache hit rate: 12% -> 35% after priming.

sam: starting step 2 -> 25% weight to green in eu-west now.

deploy-bot: traffic shift to green: eu-west 25% complete. state=stable. metrics: error_rate=0.12%, p95=120ms.

iris: confirming logs look clean, no new 5xx, CPU on green nodes 42%.

mike: rolling to 50% in 5m if no regressions. also enabling longer connection draining on blue to avoid KV cache cold misses.

nisha: alert hooks: #incidents pager on-call is ben. Setting temporary runbook reference: /runbooks/bluegreen-quick-rollback (link).

deploy-bot: scheduled automatic check at +10m for rollback conditions.

sam: bump to 50% now.

deploy-bot: traffic shift to green: eu-west 50% complete. state=stable. metrics: error_rate=0.18%, p95=130ms.

ben: seeing a small uptick in 403s from identity service (originating from green). Investigating.

olivia: can we pin requests from a few internal IPs to green for deeper traces?

mike: yes — adding header X-Internal-Trace: true for internal IP range 10.8.0.0/16.

nisha: if auth fixes take >10m, we should cut back to 25% first, not full rollback. partial drain strategy.

ben: identity team responded — a header validation tightened on green side. Patch inbound, ETA 8m.

olivia: hold at 50% and enable temporary header relaxation for green via edge rule (nudge identity).

deploy-bot: edge-rule update applied to green: relax auth header check for X-Client-ID for 10m window.

deploy-bot: metrics after relaxation: error_rate=0.09%, p95=125ms.

sam: good. continue to 100% in 10m if stable, otherwise ramp slower.

mike: remember to update LB grace period: set blue-drain to 300s, allow long-lived connections to finish.

olivia: schedule note: we'll leave blue pinned for 1h after 100% shift before decommissioning. rollback remains one-click to revert-route.

deploy-bot: shift to green: eu-west 100% complete. state=stable. metrics: error_rate=0.11%, p95=128ms.

ben: monitoring global dashboards. no regression in other regions yet.

mike: proceeding with us-west 25% now.

deploy-bot: us-west 25% -> state=stable. metrics: error_rate=0.07%, p95=115ms.

nisha: reminder: run the canary traffic generator against ru/edge and validate model outputs for sampling.

sam: doing output sampling now, looks good.

olivia: two final ops notes: 1) update release notes w/ version pin and rollback criteria, 2) flag customer-facing change window: 11:30–13:30 UTC.

ben: noted, I've posted the short customer message in help channel.

iris: will keep the runbook open and shepherd the wait period.

deploy-bot: shift job shft-2060012345 completed for all regions. green is primary. blue pools left draining for 1h.

olivia: thanks everyone — postmortem if we see any drifts. :thumbsup:
